title: THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE
text:
LATER DEVELOPMENT OF THE SAVOY PUBLIC SCHOOLS

The Savoy school continued a progressive development. The wooden structure built subsequent to the fire of 1890 was, in course of time, replaced by a modern brick building. When this building, in a few years, became both unsafe and inadequate for the district's needs, the commodious structure which now stands in Savoy was erected. The present building is modern in equipment, with gas heating, electric lights, and drinking fountains. The school has a good library, laboratory, and an auditorium. The district has incorporated several of the surrounding communities through annexation or consolidation with outlying districts, and now maintains three buses to transport the rural children to school. There is now an average enrollment of 275 pupils. Both white and colored schools have efficient teachers.

Mr. W. F. Carter is president of the present School Board. The current faculty listing with subjects taught and the number of years in Savoy follow:

Mr. J. W. Moulton, Superintendent, nine years, Latin.
Mr. Walter McCollum, principal, two years, Science and History.
Miss Alma Witherspoon, two years, English.
Miss Pauline Barnett, three years, History and Commercial Work.
Mr. Tom Garner, one year, Sixth and Seventh Grades.
Mrs. Mary Morgan, twelve years, Fourth and Fifth Grades.
Mrs. Lakah Baker, twelve years, Second and Third Grades.
Miss Beulah Fulson, fourteen years, Primary.
Mr. K. Y. Edwards, two years, Vocational Agriculture.
Miss Tommie Chesworth (daughter of T. J. Chesworth, one of the founders of Savoy College), three years, Music.
Miss Bonnie Lee Roberts, three years, Librarian.
Irene Carr, colored teacher, three years.**
